assertions.name: authorization fence: native member add, role update, remove, rejoin and leave retain one subject and pending revisions
authorization fence: public bulk member delete and native organization delete retain inactive pairs and terminal org fences
authorization fence: single and bulk native session deletion fan out across every retained pair without changing membership state
authorization fence: zero rows, equal roles and concurrent guarded role predicates produce no invented revisions
authorization fence: missing retained rows and forced revision overflow roll back native rows and every other fence
authorization backfill: rows that predate the fence tables are backfilled for their own organization on first use; sign-out and member removal then move exactly their fences
authorization backfill: a rerun adds nothing and never resets an advanced, inactive, stopped or deleted fence
authorization backfill: two runs held after reading the same candidates converge on one row per pair
authorization fence: the production organization routes create and move fences in the batches that write the native rows
authorization backfill: the workerd deploy step is a server-only management method and idempotent
relay: non-canonical JSON reaches central byte for byte on all three routes, and each verifies
relay: a body changed after signing is refused on intent while the original passes; a proof for the relay URL is refused on htu
relay: a cookie, a Bearer scheme or a missing DPoP proof is refused at the relay with valid inputs, and nothing reaches central
relay: over an expired stamp renewal cannot replace, the relay answers 503 and reaches no central admin route; once the re-sent stamp lands the same request is relayed
relay: a renewal central never answers ends at its deadline; with nothing pending the relay over a valid stamp still goes out and over an expired one is withheld (D7)

central forgot (WS7 R-notdue, R-floors): after central restarts empty, a ready organization that is not due recovers on its next relayed call; one 503, one fresh setup, its floors pushed again, and the retry is answered
R-retrysignal (relay): after an emptied central recovers, the relayed retry carries the run deadline to the link and is aborted there; the first send carries none
fleet CLI: loopback sign-in binds the token and refresh credential to the CLI key; commands go through the relay; refresh needs no browser
fleet CLI: with Keychain custody each fresh store instance (a later CLI run's store over one shared stand-in keychain) refreshes from the credential the previous one rotated, same key, no fallback
fleet CLI: a refresh with another key is invalid_dpop_proof and leaves the credential usable; after native sign-out the refresh is invalid_grant with no credential
fleet CLI snapshot probe: once the session row is gone the refresh is invalid_grant with no credential, and the CLI clears its store
fleet CLI: after a stale factor, a real app confirmation, a same-key refresh and one retry apply once; a cancelled confirmation refreshes and retries nothing
people: an unavailable outer backing call returns 503 before native captcha or state effects
people: changing spoofed XFF leaves native counting on the trusted host address
people: social starts hit the native limit and the real outer counter (Miniflare binding, Node counter) without more stored effects, and another address still passes
people: the service own page reaches the real outer counter (Miniflare binding, Node counter) without a write, and another address still passes
people: five failed recovery codes reach native verification and the sixth is limited without another intent or stamp
people: the token endpoint counts refused clients and limits the thirty-first request without minting or storing anything
